candidates.name: Ned Lamont
candidates.background: Governor since 2019, re-elected in 2022 with 56%; founded and sold the campus cable company Campus Televideo before politics and forgoes his state salary. First rose to prominence beating Sen. Joe Lieberman in the 2006 Democratic Senate primary. Survived his first primary challenge in decades, defeating progressive state Rep. Josh Elliott by more than a 2-1 margin on Aug 11.
priorities: Lowering costs of housing, electricity, healthcare, and higher education
Fiscal discipline and continued budget surpluses
Protecting reproductive rights and immigrant communities

cost.label: Capped insulin costs at $25 per month and launched energy assistance programs cutting utility bills by hundreds of dollars a year (campaign site)

health.label: Created the Covered Connecticut program giving no-cost health coverage, including dental, to nearly 40,000 adults, and has proposed a Connecticut Option public plan (campaign site)

housing.label: Mixed: passed legislation promoting new construction near mass transit and reuse of existing buildings, paired with affordable options for seniors and working families (campaign site)

immigration.label: 'Expanded and strengthened Connecticut's TRUST Act with stronger legal protections for immigrant communities' (campaign site)

taxes.label: Mixed: open to raising taxes on the wealthy 'Only when you need it', but rejects Elliott's surtax push now, warning CT income tax 'would be almost the highest if Josh has his way' (CT Mirror debate coverage)

climate.label: Set a 100% zero-carbon electric grid goal by 2040 and launched Revolution Wind to power 350,000 homes (campaign site)

education.label: Prioritizes fully funding the Education Cost Sharing formula and expanding early childhood programs, citing research that early childhood investment pays back many times over (Ballotpedia, 2018 campaign)

safety.label: Backs Project Longevity community violence prevention, citing a 21% decrease in total shootings per month in New Haven (Ballotpedia)

repro.label: 'Enacted the nation's first law after Roe v. Wade was overturned, establishing Connecticut as a safe haven' for reproductive care (campaign site)

democracy.label: Signed the no-excuse absentee voting law: 'We should be doing everything we can to encourage qualified voters to participate in elections' (CT.gov press release)

candidates.name: Ryan Fazio
candidates.background: State senator from Greenwich since a 2021 special election; Northwestern economics graduate who worked as a commodities trader and in renewable energy before politics. Won the Republican nomination at the May 16 convention with roughly 92% of delegates after former New Britain Mayor Erin Stewart suspended her campaign, avoiding a primary. Has said he voted for Trump in 2016, 2020 and 2024.
priorities: Cut electricity bills by 20%
Cut income taxes by $1,500 for every family
Restore proactive policing and public safety

cost.label: Pledges to 'cut electricity bills by 20%' by ending hidden taxes and removing cost-driving mandates, plus a $1,500 income tax cut for every family (campaign site)

health.label: Would increase healthcare access and jobs by 'improving state rules and regulations' rather than expanding public programs (Ballotpedia)

housing.label: Mixed: defends local zoning control while saying 'I support accessory dwelling units, mixed-use residential development, and sensible workforce housing' (Senate Republicans release, Feb 2026)

immigration.label: Will 'reduce taxpayer spending on illegal immigration and reverse the 2019 sanctuary state policies' (campaign site)

taxes.label: Pledges to 'slash income tax rates for all families for the first time in state history' while cutting 'wasteful spending' and reforming state employee packages (Ballotpedia)

climate.label: Energy plan centers on cutting electricity bills by 'ending hidden taxes, expanding reliable supply, and removing the mandates driving up costs' (campaign site)

education.label: Supports 'more choice to poor kids stuck in failing schools', higher K-12 standards with local control, and a state university tuition freeze (Ballotpedia)

safety.label: Plan 'reforms the 2020 anti-police legislation, closes parole loopholes for violent offenders, and reinstates proactive policing' (campaign site)

repro.label: Mixed: says 'restricting abortion in Connecticut is never going to happen' and backs the state's guarantee, but opposed the 2022 safe-harbor law protecting patients from out-of-state abortion prosecutions (CT Mirror)

democracy.label: Opposed Connecticut's 2022 early voting referendum: 'Connecticut state law already effectively provides early voting', long voting periods let 'groups and parties effectively harvest votes' and diminish 'the value of Election Day' (Stamford Elections questionnaire, 2022)

sources.label: CT Mirror: Democratic primary result and general matchup

candidates.name: Luke Bronin
candidates.background: Two-term mayor of Hartford (2016 to 2024), earlier general counsel to Gov. Dannel Malloy and a Treasury official in the Obama administration; Navy intelligence officer who deployed to Afghanistan on an anti-corruption task force, and a Rhodes Scholar. Suspended a 2018 run for governor. Won the Aug. 11, 2026 Democratic primary with 53.5% over 14-term Rep. John Larson (34.7%), so there is no incumbent on the November ballot.
priorities: Bringing down costs: housing, health care, energy, child and elder care
A public Medicare option and drug price negotiation
A progressive tax code and getting dark money out of politics

cost.label: Mixed: wants Medicare and Medicaid to negotiate drug prices and 'investments that the private sector won't make', but also 'fixing bottlenecks that artificially drive up prices, from permitting delays to outdated regulations' (campaign site)

health.label: Backs 'a strong public option so that any American who wants to participate in Medicare can do so', drug price negotiation and breaking up 'healthcare monopolies' (campaign site)

housing.label: 'We need more flexible federal financing tools, to help communities build a mix of market rate and affordable housing' and 'slumlords and absentee-landlords can be held accountable' (campaign site)

immigration.label: Wants 'legal pathways that encourage more legal immigration' and 'citizenship for DACA recipients', would 'Abolish ICE', while also backing 'secure borders, fair and timely asylum processing' (campaign site)

taxes.label: Roll back Trump-era cuts for high earners, add 'two new top income tax brackets', restore the corporate rate to '35% or at minimum to 28%', raise estate taxes and tax capital gains 'closer to ordinary income' (campaign site)

climate.label: 'We need a massive commitment to more affordable, clean energy. Solar, wind, hydro, fuel cells, nuclear', with 'smart public investments to accelerate the transition'; faults Trump for 'doubling down on dirty and inefficient fossil fuels' (campaign site)

education.label: 'We should invest more in people, with smaller class sizes, stronger teacher training and recruitment, better teacher pay', from early childhood through college (campaign site)

safety.label: Mixed: will 'support vital community violence prevention work like violence interrupters and hospital-based violence intervention programs' and as mayor 'also demanded real accountability for people involved in gun violence' (campaign site)

repro.label: 'Roe v Wade must be codified in federal law'; as mayor led one of the first ordinances against 'the abuses of crisis pregnancy centers' (campaign site)

nullNotes.democracy: checked campaign issues index and Fighting Corruption page (overturn Citizens United, limit pardon power, ban congressional stock trading), Ballotpedia (no Candidate Connection survey), CT Mirror primary coverage; nothing on voter registration, mail or early voting, or voter ID, and campaign finance items do not fit the axis

candidates.name: Amy Fogelstrom Chai
candidates.now: Physician, internal medicine and addiction medicine
candidates.background: Detroit-born physician (Indiana University School of Medicine, 1989) with a master's in epidemiology, author and mental health advocate. Ran for Congress in the 3rd District in 2022 as an independent, taking 1.7% against Rep. Rosa DeLauro. Announced a Republican bid for the 1st District in January 2026 with the slogan 'listen more, hate less' and a platform of prevention, transparency in government spending and term limits; is the GOP nominee against Luke Bronin.
priorities: Prevention of mental illness and addiction
Transparency in federal spending and the national debt
Parental rights and literacy in schools

health.label: Mixed: 'With passage of the ACA, the costs of healthcare skyrocketed', yet wants government 'caps on profits for VCs that own healthcare conglomerates' to put '2.6 trillion back in your pocket' (Ballotpedia survey)

housing.label: Has drafted federal legislation limiting private equity purchases of single-family homes and proposes a Hartford pilot for affordable homeownership on underutilized properties; 'Investors are using the low-income housing market for profit' (CT Mirror)

immigration.label: 'I do not believe that a US Representative should impede the enforcement of border security, ever' (Ballotpedia survey)

taxes.label: Mixed: 'Property taxes must be capped', the self-employment tax 'must be eliminated' and 'We must spend less', but also 'More tax on financial industry and less tax on earned income' (campaign site)

climate.label: Mixed: 'I would like to present a better option for America than the Green New Deal', proposing locally sourced 'Sustainability Zones' for food, energy and medicine, innovation over top-down mandates (Ballotpedia survey, 2022 and 2025)

education.label: 'Parents have every right to determine what their children are learning, whether it be through public schools or home education'; wants classroom curriculum disclosure (campaign site)

safety.label: 'Prevention over reaction': address 'the root causes of mental illness, addiction, crime and poverty' and prioritize 'reintegration of ex-offenders' (New Britain Herald)

democracy.label: 'I would create federal standards with requirements for voter ID and careful monitoring of voter rolls', 'a maximum of one week of early voting' and paper ballots; also backs ranked choice voting (Ballotpedia survey)

nullNotes.cost: checked campaign issues page (Prosperity section is about small business and 'local self-sufficiency' with no price, subsidy, wage or deregulation mechanism), Ballotpedia survey, New Britain Herald and Bristol Press announcements, Patch 2022 profile; nothing that fits the axis
nullNotes.repro: checked campaign issues page, Ballotpedia 2022 and 2025 surveys, Patch 2022 profile, Hartford Courant 2022 profile, iVoterGuide 2022 (she left the abortion question unanswered); no abortion position anywhere

candidates.name: Jim Himes
candidates.now: U.S. Representative, CT-4 (since 2009); Ranking Member, House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence
candidates.background: Born in Lima, Peru to American parents; Harvard graduate and Rhodes Scholar. Spent 12 years at Goldman Sachs, then ran the New York office of Enterprise Community Partners, an affordable-housing nonprofit, and chaired the Greenwich Housing Authority. Elected to Congress in 2008 and now in his ninth term; sits on Financial Services and is the top Democrat on the Intelligence Committee. Beat Michael Goldstein 61% to 37% in 2024 and faces him again in November 2026.
priorities: Lowering health care and prescription drug costs
Climate action and clean energy
Protecting democracy and voting rights

cost.label: Has 'supported measures that decrease prescription drug costs, cap insulin prices' (himes.house.gov health care page)

health.label: 'The Affordable Care Act put our country on the right path'; backs measures to 'expand health insurance subsidies' and 'expand eligibility for insurance coverage' (himes.house.gov health care page)

housing.label: Voted Jan. 31, 2024 for the Tax Relief for American Families and Workers Act to 'expand the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit' and 'accelerate the construction of affordable housing' (himes.house.gov press release)

immigration.label: Voted Nay on passage of S.5, the Laken Riley Act, Jan. 22, 2025, roll call 23 (clerk.house.gov)

taxes.label: Voted No on concurring in the Senate amendment to H.R.1, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, July 3, 2025, roll call 190, the Republican reconciliation bill extending the 2017 tax cuts (clerk.house.gov)

climate.label: 'A fully-refundable carbon fee would correct this market failure by shifting the cost to emitters'; 'the urgency to transition to clean energy has never been greater'; voted for the Inflation Reduction Act (himes.house.gov climate page)

education.label: 'We must ensure our public schools are robustly funded'; has backed fully funding IDEA and increased Title I investment (himes.house.gov education page)

repro.label: 'Longtime supporter of the Women's Health Protection Act... enshrining protection to abortion access into federal law' (himes.house.gov reproductive freedom page)

democracy.label: 'The John R. Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act, which I am proud to have co-sponsored and voted for, would restore federal oversight of state and local voting policies' (himes.house.gov voting rights page)

sources.label: Patch: 2026 CT-4 Republican primary result (Goldstein nominated to face Himes)

nullNotes.safety: checked himes.house.gov issues index (only a gun violence prevention page, which does not count for this axis), 2024 press releases on police department grants and a reentry health grant (both routine grant announcements, which do not count under the calibration rule), CT Mirror 2024 debate coverage; no statement for or against enforcement versus prevention

candidates.name: Michael Goldstein
candidates.now: Ophthalmic surgeon and attorney; former member, Greenwich Representative Town Meeting
candidates.background: New York City native and Greenwich resident since 1987; M.D. from SUNY Downstate (1974) and J.D. from Pace Law (2006), and is a past president of the New York County Medical Society. Lost the 2022 GOP primary, then won the 2024 nomination and lost to Himes 61% to 37%. Won the Aug. 11, 2026 Republican primary over Dan Miressi with 73% (4,628 to 1,606) for a rematch with Himes.
priorities: Cut health care regulation and restore competition to lower costs
Lower Connecticut electricity bills via natural gas pipelines and nuclear
Career pathways: trade schools, apprenticeships, student debt relief for graduates who stay in CT

cost.label: On drug prices, mixed: the government 'should build upon that framework' of IRA Medicare price negotiation, while 'streamlining the regulatory process, encouraging biosimilars and generics' and reforming PBMs to cut costs (Nancy on Norwalk questionnaire)

health.label: Cites Democratic proposals like 'Medicare for All' as a concern and says 'health care needs more competition and choice' (CT Mirror)

housing.label: '21st Century Homestead Act' mixes 'Down payment assistance' and first-time-buyer tax incentives with 'Streamlined permitting. Incentives for zoning reform' and cutting federal environmental review delays (campaign platform)

immigration.label: 'Ideally, there should be no illegal immigration'; wants secure borders and targeted enforcement on 'violent criminals, gang members, terrorists', with foreign workers admitted only 'through a lawful visa system' (Nancy on Norwalk questionnaire)

taxes.label: Backed extending the expiring 2017 tax provisions: 'keeping taxes low is a way to stimulating the economy... keeping more money in people's pockets is a very good idea' (CT Mirror 2024 debate)

climate.label: 'Natural gas, nuclear, and renewables. Prioritize affordability, not ideology'; 'Remove federal barriers blocking natural gas pipeline capacity into New England'; mandates forcing 'expensive energy transitions' drive up costs (campaign platform)

education.label: 'Federal funding follows the student. Education Savings Accounts give families real options'; mandates 'complete curriculum disclosure' and parental consent (campaign platform)

safety.label: 'Safe Streets, No Exceptions': federal funding for police 'hiring bonuses, retention incentives', incentives for states keeping bail for violent crimes, 'Increase penalties' on fentanyl traffickers (campaign platform)

repro.label: Disagreed that abortion access is a fundamental right: 'it is up to each state to decide and that voters should be able to vote on the issue in a referendum' (CT Mirror 2024 debate)

democracy.label: 'I also support responsible investments in election integrity. Connecticut has experienced serious concerns involving absentee ballots... The public must have confidence that... election fraud is investigated and prevented' (Nancy on Norwalk questionnaire)

nullNotes.age: Patch and CT Mirror gave 74 in October 2024; no fetched page states a birth date or current age

candidates.name: Joseph Courtney
candidates.now: U.S. Representative, CT-2 (since 2007); Ranking Member, House Armed Services Seapower Subcommittee
candidates.background: Lawyer and former Vernon town attorney who served in the Connecticut General Assembly from 1987 to 1994, chairing the Public Health and Human Services committees. First elected to Congress in 2006 and has represented eastern Connecticut since; sits on Armed Services (Ranking Member, Seapower and Projection Forces) and Education and Workforce, and co-chairs the Congressional Shipbuilding Caucus. Seeking an eleventh term in 2026 against Republican George Austin.
priorities: Submarine industrial base and Electric Boat jobs
Protecting Medicaid and ACA coverage from H.R. 1 cuts
Offshore wind and eastern Connecticut energy supply

cost.label: Called on Congress to 'pass the Health Care Affordability Act to make ACA subsidies permanent' after CT premium hikes, saying 'health insurance is already way too expensive' (Courtney press release, Sept 2025)

health.label: Denounced H.R. 1's $1 trillion Medicaid cut and its 'medical frailty' work-requirement rules as 'inhumane' on the House floor (Courtney press release, June 2026)

housing.label: Voted for the ROAD to Housing Act (396-13), a 'rare bipartisan breakthrough' pairing 'federal reforms to generate new housing construction' with measures to 'expand affordable rental housing, prevent homelessness' (Courtney press release, May 2026)

immigration.label: Voted for the Laken Riley Act detention bill ('it still left open the door for due process') but voted against H.R. 875 deportation bill and blasted DHS for dismissing 'due process as a requirement, which the 14th Amendment clearly creates for all persons' (CT Mirror)

taxes.label: Voted No on final passage of H.R. 1, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which made the 2017 tax cuts permanent (218-214) (House Clerk roll call 190, July 3, 2025)

climate.label: Fought Trump's stop-work order on the Revolution Wind offshore project, calling it 'a much-needed expansion of energy capacity' negotiated below current wind rates (Courtney press release, Aug 2025)

education.label: Opposed abolishing the Education Department, 'a major, major partner' delivering Title I money to 'nearly every K-12 public school in CT-02' and special education funding (Courtney press release, Feb 2025)

repro.label: Voted for the Women's Health Protection Act to 're-establish that Americans have a statutory right to receive abortion care' and called Dobbs 'a stunning step backwards' (Courtney press release, July 2022)

democracy.label: Voted Nay on H.R. 22, the SAVE Act, requiring documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote (passed 220-208) (House Clerk roll call 102, April 10, 2025)

nullNotes.safety: checked courtney.house.gov Public Safety and Homeland Security issues page (only fire, road-safety and public-safety grant announcements plus gun votes, which do not map to this axis) and press release list; no prevention-versus-enforcement position documented

candidates.name: George Patrick Austin
candidates.now: Small business owner in construction management
candidates.background: First-generation American who married at 17 after meeting his wife in Mexico and navigated the U.S. immigration system with her; paid his own way through Central Connecticut State University with a construction management degree and now owns a small business. Member of the Home Builders and Remodelers Association, NFIB, CCDL and NRA. Won the CT GOP nomination for the 2nd District by acclamation at the May 15, 2026 convention as the only Republican candidate. Wrote on his campaign blog in January 2026 that he is 38 years old.
priorities: Lower costs: energy bills, taxes and mandates
Trade education and apprenticeships for defense manufacturing jobs
Border security and asylum reform

cost.label: 'Deliver tax relief to keep more money in your pocket' and 'make Connecticut more competitive to attract businesses' as the answer to housing, utility and food costs (campaign site, Dollars and Sense)

health.label: Campaign blog: 'the cuts to Medicaid were necessary' and calls for 'hard conversations about any and all entitlement programs' (campaign blog, Jan 2026)

immigration.label: 'Strengthen border security and restore order' with 'physical barriers in appropriate locations', 'replace catch-and-release with consistent processing', while also modernizing legal pathways (campaign site, Securing Our Borders)

taxes.label: Promises an 'America First, limited-government approach' to 'cut waste, and stop abusing the taxpayer credit card with impunity' and fight 'high taxes' (campaign site)

climate.label: Will 'push for energy policies that lower utility bills' and refuses to 'bow to extreme green ideology that relies on shame, propaganda, and fear' (campaign site, Dollars and Sense)

education.label: Told the Lee Elci Show of 'the importance of parental choice in education, including protecting the rights of homeschooling families' and parental 'notification and transparency' (campaign site, March 2026 post)

safety.label: Spanish-language platform: 'proteger a nuestras comunidades del aumento de crímenes respaldando a la policía' (protect communities from rising crime by backing the police) (campaign site, Spanish page)

repro.label: Spanish-language platform: 'Seré defensor para los infantes en contra del aborto' (I will be a defender of infants against abortion); also describes 'my pro-life stance' in a March 2026 post (campaign site, Spanish page)

candidates.name: Rosa L Delauro
candidates.now: U.S. Representative, CT-3 (since 1991); ranking member, House Appropriations Committee
candidates.background: New Haven native who has represented Connecticut's 3rd district since 1991 and is the top Democrat on the House Appropriations Committee. Seeking a 19th term; won the May 2026 Democratic convention endorsement with about 87 percent of delegates, and challenger Andrew Rice's convention protest was rejected, leaving her without a primary. Re-elected in 2024 with 58.9 percent.
priorities: Protect Medicaid and health programs from Republican budget cuts
Expand the Child Tax Credit and lower costs for working families
Fund public schools, Title I and Head Start

cost.label: Voted for the House-passed Consumer Fuel Price Gouging Prevention Act (2022), which 'would be the first ever federal law against price gouging' (DeLauro press release)

health.label: Voted against the April 10, 2025 Republican budget resolution she said would 'gut Medicaid by $880 billion and leave 80 million Americans without healthcare' (DeLauro press release)

housing.label: Voted for the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (May 21, 2026), backing 'an all-of-the-above approach that helps us build more homes' while 'fighting against the proposed cuts to the HOME Investment Partnerships Program' (DeLauro press release)

immigration.label: Voted Nay on passage of S. 5, the Laken Riley Act, January 22, 2025 (House Clerk roll 23)

taxes.label: Backs a tax code 'asking the wealthiest Americans to pay their share': return rates on the wealthiest 2 percent to Clinton-era levels, the 'Buffett Rule', and end 'tax breaks for companies that ship jobs overseas' (DeLauro issues page)

climate.label: Wants to 'shift away from fossil fuels and diversify with investments in the next generation of clean and renewable energy technologies'; supported the Inflation Reduction Act's emissions cuts (DeLauro issues page)

education.label: 'Ensuring our public schools are given the resources and the support they need is among government's central obligations'; fought to fully fund Title I and Head Start and introduced the CHARTER Act to keep federal funds from for-profit-run charters (DeLauro issues page)

safety.label: Mixed: opposed the FY2026 CJS bill both because it 'defunds federal law enforcement' and freezes COPS grants, and because it cuts 'reentry initiatives and violence prevention' and 'Community Violence Intervention and Prevention grants' (Appropriations Democrats remarks, Sept. 10, 2025)

repro.label: Voted for the Women's Health Protection Act and Ensuring Access to Abortion Act: 'Access to abortion is a fundamental right' (DeLauro press release)

democracy.label: Voted Nay on passage of H.R. 22, the SAVE Act, April 10, 2025 (House Clerk roll 102)

sources.label: CT Mirror: DeLauro convention win upheld
House Clerk roll 190: voted No on H.R. 1 One Big Beautiful Bill Act, July 3, 2025

candidates.name: Christopher John Lancia
candidates.now: Outside plant manager at TNI, a fiber network provider; U.S. Coast Guard veteran and former federal law enforcement officer
candidates.background: Bridgeport native and 1989 Central High School graduate now living in Milford. Border security
Parental rights in schools and term limits

immigration.label: 'We must control our borders to stop the flow of drugs and crime into our towns'; calls border security national security (campaign site)

taxes.label: Platform lists 'lower taxes and fewer regulations to help small businesses thrive' and 'real accountability for wasteful government spending' (Joe Hoft)

climate.label: Platform lists 'energy independence to bring down Connecticut's sky-high utility bills' (Joe Hoft)

education.label: 'Parents, not bureaucrats, should make decisions for their children. Schools should focus on academics, not agendas' (campaign site)

Public education and support for teachers

candidates.name: Chris Shea
candidates.now: Lieutenant, North Haven Fire Department; retired Navy SEAL
candidates.background: Watertown native, retired Navy SEAL with more than 30 years of service who retired in January 2024, and a North Haven firefighter since 2009. Founded Hero to Hero, a nonprofit that helps veterans move into first-responder careers, and previously ran a small handyman business. First run for office; won the August 11, 2026 Republican primary over Jonathan De Barros with about 80% of the vote.
priorities: Lowering the cost of living, energy bills and taxes
Securing the border and stopping illegal immigration and fentanyl
Supporting veterans

cost.label: Names 'high energy costs and overregulation' as the burdens on Connecticut's economy and working families (campaign site)

immigration.label: 'Chris will always fight to secure the border, enforce our immigration laws, and stop the flow of fentanyl' (campaign site)

taxes.label: Defends the 2025 'Big Beautiful Bill' tax cuts and faults Hayes for voting against 'the SALT deduction' and the tips and overtime deductions his 'firefighter and police buddies' will get (WTNH)

safety.label: Pledges to 'support law enforcement, and put the safety of American families first' and to 'crack down on the flow of drugs and crime' (campaign site)

housing.label: On 'rising housing costs': will 'promote practical housing solutions' by 'reducing unnecessary barriers that drive up costs' (campaign site)
